children: and Nigerian partner Amni said Wednesday they have taken a final investment decision to
the Ima gas field offshore Nigeria, which will supply a Nigeria LNG liquefaction ​plant.

said the Ima field will be developed with a single platform, connected through a 22-km pipeline to Nigeria LNG; the field is expected to begin production in 2028 and reach a plateau of 350M cf/day, equivalent to more than 60K boe/day.

Once on stream, the Ima field will supply about one-third of the gas required for the ongoing Nigeria LNG Train 7 expansion project, which will increase the liquefaction plant capacity to 30M metric tons/year from 22M tons/year currently.
Ima is a low-cost and low-emissions development, with a simplified platform design, electric power supply from shore, no flaring, and permanent methane detection and monitoring.
Amni owns a 60% stake in the field, and TotalEnergies
is the operator and holds a 40% stake.

title: TotalEnergies, partner approve development of Ima gas field offshore Nigeria
